text:
jeff: heads-up — I hit a weird cancellation bug in the Go sample app for generator streaming. ctx.Done() doesn't stop the streaming goroutine, tokens keep coming for ~2s after cancel.

anna: oof. which sample app? the hello-generator one?

jeff: yeah the sample generator used in devex-example. repro steps: start stream, then cancel parent ctx immediately. stream still writes until EOF.

mike: is this the same as the earlier ctx propagation mismatch we saw with the v2 client?

jeff: similar surface but different cause. looks like our internal backlog flush waits on the transport write to finish even after ctx cancels. gist:

jeff: ```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
stream, _ := client.Generator(ctx, req)
go func() {
  time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
  cancel()
}()
for {
  tok, err := stream.Recv() // this keeps returning tokens for ~2s
  if err != nil { break }
  // process
}
```

anna: can you paste the client config? maybe ReadDeadline or http transport settings delaying cancellation?

jeff: default http transport, nothing fancy. Also tried injecting ctx into transport.RoundTripper and CancelRequest works, but generator has an internal batching loop that drains the send queue before returning.

mike: ah, batching loop. If the runtime queues a few requests and flushes on a ticker, canceling ctx might not interrupt the ticker-driven flush.

jeff: exactly. quick hack in sample: check ctx.Done() inside batching loop and return early. fixes UX but feels like band-aid. we probably need a contract: generator.Recv should return on ctx cancel immediately.

anna: agree. two options: 1) make transport writes cancelable via request contexts (more invasive), or 2) add explicit ctx checks in the generator loop and prefer early exit. leaning to 2 for DX surface.

mike: +1 for 2 as a short-term fix. also add a unit test that cancels and asserts Recv returns within 50ms. non-flaky if we stub network.

jeff: i'll implement PR with tests. question: behavior across stream streaming vs unary generation — parity matters. do we treat generator streams the same as streaming chat cancel semantics?

anna: yes, SDK parity win: same cancel semantics for generator and chat streaming. doc note too.

jeff: ok I'll include changelog + sample app update demonstrating cancel pattern.

ci-bot: CI queued — jeff/generator-cancel-fix #branch created by jeff.

mike: one more ask — add a small example in README showing `defer cancel()` and an explicit timeout for long-running clients. new users keep forgetting. :pray:

jeff: will do. thanks folks.

anna: thanks — happy to review the PR. :thumbsup:
